roles_en: Ambassador of the Republic of Armenia
bio_en: Mikayel Hovhannisian, who took the pen-name Varandian after 1900, was born around 1871 in Kyotuk in the Varanda district of Karabakh and grew up in Shushi, graduating from the Russian Realschule. He studied sociology, history and philosophy mainly at the University of Geneva and from his student years wrote for Mshak and the ARF organ Droshak. He wrote major works including 'The ARF and its opponents' and 'The prehistory of the Armenian movement', took part in Khrimian Hayrik's national congress of 1906, and was a member of the ARF Bureau from 1907. Elected to Armenia's first parliament, he served as ambassador in Rome in 1919-22; he died in 1934.
